title: 475 dates x 6 speeds have no audio on archive.org (Oct 2024 - Jan 2026)
description:
Measured 2026-11-09 against https://archive.org/metadata/mcp.NN.WPM for all six speeds vs the 2063 posts on github/main:

  2021 posts=290 missing=2
  2022 posts=365 missing=2
  2023 posts=365 missing=1
  2024 posts=366 missing=82
  2025 posts=365 missing=365   <-- entire year
  2026 posts=312 missing=23    <-- all before 2026-01-24

1591 mp3s exist per item, 475 dates are absent. Confirmed 404 at
archive.org/download/ for 2021-03-16, 2022-02-06, 2025-06-15.

Posts for those dates exist in _posts and were listed in the feed with
length="0" before 91d19ff7. _includes/feed.xml now skips them, so a NEW
subscriber sees a clean 100-item window (2026-08-01..2026-11-08, all
enclosures verified 200 with Content-Length matching the advertised
length). But AntennaPod keeps items in its local DB forever, so a
subscription predating the fix still holds ~475 items whose enclosures
404 and retries them on every refresh. That is the reported 'fails every
time, reliably'.

Fix = press and upload the missing dates. The show-note text is already
in each post front matter (message:), so the audio is reproducible.
acceptance_criteria: archive.org/metadata/mcp.NN.WPM lists an mp3 for every date in _posts, for all six speeds. backfill_metadata.py reports 'posts with no audio on archive.org: 0'.

title: Fix podcast feed metadata so AntennaPod can download episodes
description: All six rss/*WPM.xml feeds advertise false/invalid enclosure metadata: type=audio/mp3 (unregistered; archive.org serves audio/mpeg), length=11444 hardcoded on all 2028 items (real files 400KB-2MB), itunes:duration=01:00 hardcoded. Channel artwork /images/itunes.png is 404. _config.yml missing author/email/lang/keywords so language, managingEditor, itunes:owner/email render empty. Invalid iTunes categories. No item cap (1.97MB x 6 feeds).
close_reason: Fixed in 91d19ff. audio/mpeg, real per-speed length/duration from archive.org metadata, artwork added, language/author/keywords set, valid categories, 100-item cap, items with missing audio omitted. Live feeds verified: 36 enclosures spot-checked, all 200 with Content-Length matching declared size.

title: verify_feeds.py: check every enclosure against archive.org metadata, not 3 random HEADs
description:
The pre-deploy gate currently picks 3 random enclosures per feed and HEADs them (18 requests, probabilistic). A feed with one bad item passes 97 times out of 100.

archive.org publishes every file's name and size in one metadata document per item -- the same six requests backfill_metadata.py and now episode_press.sh already make. Use those instead: assert EVERY item's enclosure exists in the item and that its declared length matches the recorded size.

Same request count, full coverage, no sampling luck, and it is the gate that stops a feed advertising audio that is not there from ever deploying again. Keep the existing upstream-outage tolerance: archive.org being unreachable is not a defect in our feed and must stay a warning, not a failure.
acceptance_criteria: verify_feeds.py makes 6 archive.org requests and validates 100% of items in all six feeds. Deliberately corrupting one length_NN in a post makes the gate fail. An unreachable archive.org still warns rather than fails.

title: Daily run repairs the N newest missing dates instead of a bulk backfill
description:
User declined a bulk backfill of the 475-date gap (2026-11-09): 'I don't want to backfill those dates because that'd be an insane amount of stuff to push at once.'

Replace the chunked manual-dispatch workflow (-nco, superseded) with a bounded repair inside the existing daily run: after the 7-day window, press the N NEWEST dates that have no audio, default N=3.

Newest-first on purpose. The feed shows the newest 100 items that HAVE audio, which today reaches back to 2026-08-01, so filling a 2025 date changes nothing a new subscriber sees. The only thing the repair fixes is the enclosure URLs that existing clients already hold and keep retrying -- and the most recently broken ones (Jan 2026, late 2024) are the ones still live in those clients.

Self-limiting: does nothing once the gap is zero. 475 dates at 3/run is ~5 months, +~3 min of runner time per day, no burst. N is the only knob.

Depends on the explicit date list (-72b) and the metadata existence set (-2qm, done).
acceptance_criteria: A daily run with the gap non-empty presses exactly N extra dates, newest-missing-first, and uploads 6N files. With an empty gap it presses nothing and the run time is unchanged. A test case in test_episode_press.sh covers both.

title: episode_press.sh: one /metadata/ fetch per item instead of per-date HEAD requests
description:
check_episode_exists() does one HEAD to archive.org/download/ per (date,wpm). The 7-day window costs 42 requests per run, which is fine, but a 475-date backfill would cost 2850 HEADs and get throttled.

backfill_metadata.py already proves the cheap way: one GET to archive.org/metadata/mcp.NN.WPM returns every file in the item. Six requests covers any number of dates.

Build the existence set once at startup, look dates up in it. Keep check_episode_exists as the lookup seam so test_episode_press.sh's curl stub still works, or extend the stub.
acceptance_criteria: A backfill over N dates makes 6 archive.org metadata requests, not 6N HEADs. test_episode_press.sh still passes.
close_reason: prefetch_existing_audio() reads archive.org/metadata once per speed; check_episode_exists answers from the set. 6 requests per run, was 42. 17/17 press tests pass.

title: episode_press.sh: accept an explicit date list for historical backfill
description:
main() hardcodes a 7-day sliding window (MAX_BACKFILL_DAYS). The 475-date gap from Oct 2024 to Jan 2026 is outside it and can never self-heal.

Add an opt-in date list (env var or positional --dates) that replaces the window and reuses process_date() unchanged. Dates whose post already exists must reuse the stored message: front matter, never call fortune -- regenerating the show note would make the audio disagree with the published post text.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing an explicit 2025 date uploads six mp3s built from that post's existing message: text and leaves the post file byte-identical. Covered by a test_episode_press.sh case.
close_reason: BACKFILL_DATES env var replaces the window for one run; validated YYYY-MM-DD; two new cases in test_episode_press.sh (30/30 pass)

title: CI: fortune data missing after --no-install-recommends
description: Scheduled build failed every day 2026-10-06..2026-10-12. fortune-mod ships no data; fortunes-min is only a Recommends, skipped by --no-install-recommends added in 4aa25db7. fortune -s exited 1, set -e aborted episode_press.sh on the oldest backfill date, blocking all newer dates. report job mislabeled it as upload failures.
close_reason: fortunes-min installed explicitly + fortune smoke check in CI; per-date failure isolation in episode_press.sh; report job message corrected

title: Feed GUIDs are identical across all six WPM feeds
description:
_includes/feed.xml emits <guid isPermaLink="true">{{ site.url }}{{ post.url }}</guid> with no WPM discriminator, so 2026-11-08 has the same GUID in 05WPM.xml and in 30WPM.xml.

Per-feed-dedup clients (AntennaPod) are unaffected. Clients that key episodes globally (some CLI aggregators, directory ingesters) will treat the six speeds as one episode. Low blast radius but wrong.

Changing GUIDs makes every client re-ingest the whole 100-item window once, so land it deliberately, not as a drive-by.
acceptance_criteria: Each feed's GUIDs are unique to that feed; verify_feeds.py asserts no GUID appears in two feeds.
notes: Deferred 2026-11-09 at user direction: changing GUIDs makes every client re-ingest the current 100-item window once, which looks like 100 new episodes. Not worth a visible blip for a purity fix nobody reported. Revisit if a directory or CLI aggregator actually collapses the six speeds.

title: Chunked manual-dispatch workflow to press the archive.org gap
description:
One date is ~67s for six speeds (measured, run 42631326387 step 9). 475 dates is ~9h of runner time, over the 6h per-job cap.

Add .github/workflows/backfill.yml: workflow_dispatch with a chunk-size input, computes the missing dates from archive.org metadata vs _posts, presses the first N, exits. Must not collide with the daily build -- reuse concurrency group 'build'. Do not add a schedule; this is a one-off catch-up, re-dispatched until the gap is zero.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch with chunk=20 presses 20 missing dates, uploads 120 files, and does not race the daily build.

title: Modernize CI: native Pages deploy, shallow clone, conditional build deps
description: build.yml inefficiencies: fetch-depth=0 full-clones a repo with 2000+ posts and 240+ bot commits; build-essential/gettext/libvorbis-dev/libmp3lame-dev installed every run though only needed on ebook2cw cache miss; gh-pages deploy rewrites the entire site as a new commit daily, bloating the branch forever. Replace with actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages, shallow fetch, cache-conditional apt, concurrency group, .jekyll-cache caching.
close_reason: Done in 91d19ff except the native Pages migration, which needs the repo Pages source flipped from legacy/gh-pages to workflow. Landed: shallow checkout, toolchain packages only on ebook2cw cache miss, jekyll cache, concurrency group, dedicated gh-pages checkout replacing the clean -fdx/orphan dance, feed-verification gate.

title: Migrate GitHub Pages to native Actions deploy
description: Repo Pages is build_type=legacy with source branch gh-pages, so every daily build commits the entire rendered site as a new commit, growing that branch forever. Switching to actions/upload-pages-artifact + actions/deploy-pages removes the gh-pages branch entirely. Requires flipping the Pages source to 'GitHub Actions' (PUT /repos/:owner/:repo/pages with build_type=workflow) in the same change, or deploys break.
close_reason: Done. Pages build_type flipped legacy->workflow; workflow split into build/deploy/report with actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5 + actions/deploy-pages@v5; all gh-pages logic removed and the gh-pages branch deleted (was 177f7933). Native deployment 6869231332 (sha ff0d0444) succeeded and is serving live: all six feeds 200/100 items, artwork 200, index 200. Also landed: jekyll 4.2->4.4.1, ruby 3.2->3.4, committed Gemfile.lock, jekyll-timeago dropped, action SHA pins, ubuntu-24.04 pin, ebook2cw pinned to b4b1fa2d, dependabot for actions+bundler, and _config.yml exclude for repo files that were publicly served.
